title: The Rib Cage
question: Which part of the breastbone is it?
lines: The breastbone has three parts. Can you name this one?
Look at the long, flat part in the middle of the breastbone.
Which part of the breastbone is glowing?
The manubrium is the wide top, and the xiphoid is the small tip.
This long, flat part makes up most of the breastbone.
It's C. The body of the sternum.
Why it matters: several ribs link to it through cartilage.

title: The Rib Cage
question: Which group of ribs is glowing?
lines: Seven rib pairs attach straight to the breastbone. Which group?
Watch the glowing ribs in the upper part of the chest.
Which group of ribs is glowing?
False ribs reach the breastbone only through shared cartilage.
Ribs 1 to 7 each have their own cartilage link to the breastbone.
It's D. The true ribs.
Why it matters: they form the sturdy upper cage around heart and lungs.

title: The Rib Cage
question: What's its everyday name?
lines: Tap the middle of your chest. That flat bone has an everyday name.
Watch the glowing bone down the center of the rib cage.
What's its everyday name?
The collarbone is higher up, across the base of the neck.
This one runs down the middle, joined to the ribs by cartilage.
It's A. The breastbone, or sternum.
Why it matters: it anchors the front of the rib cage.

title: The Rib Cage
question: How many ribs are glowing in all?
lines: Some of your ribs only attach at the back. They float.
Watch the glowing ribs at the bottom of the cage.
How many ribs are glowing in all?
These are the floating ribs, ribs 11 and 12 on each side.
Two on the left and two on the right.
It's B. Four floating ribs.
Why it matters: their front ends are free, not joined to the breastbone.

title: The Rib Cage
question: How many pairs of ribs do we have?
lines: Men and women have the same number of ribs. How many pairs?
Watch every glowing rib around the chest.
How many pairs of ribs do we have?
Twenty-four is the number of ribs in all, two per pair.
Twelve pairs, one on each side of the chest.
It's B. Twelve pairs.
Why it matters: together they protect the heart and lungs.

title: The Rib Cage
question: Which part of the breastbone is it?
lines: Your breastbone has three parts. Can you name this one?
Look at the glowing piece at the top of the breastbone.
Which part of the breastbone is it?
The long middle part is the body. The tip is the xiphoid process.
It's C. The manubrium.
Why it matters: your collarbones and first ribs attach to it.

title: The Rib Cage
question: What is the small tip of the breastbone?
lines: At the bottom of your breastbone is a small pointed tip.
Watch the glowing tip at the lower end of the sternum.
What is the small tip of the breastbone?
The body of the sternum is the long middle part above it.
This small pointed piece is the lowest part of the breastbone.
It's A. The xiphoid process.
Why it matters: it's the sternum's third part, below the body.

title: The Rib Cage
question: What joins the upper ribs to the sternum?
lines: Your ribs don't touch your breastbone directly. Something sits between.
Watch the glowing bands between ribs and breastbone.
What tissue joins the upper ribs to the breastbone?
A tendon links muscle to bone, not rib to breastbone.
This flexible tissue is cartilage.
It's B. Costal cartilage.
Why it matters: it lets your rib cage expand when you breathe.

title: The Rib Cage
question: Which pair of ribs is glowing?
lines: One pair of ribs sits right below your collarbones.
Watch the glowing ribs at the very top of the cage.
Which pair of ribs is glowing?
The second ribs are longer and less curved.
These are the shortest, broadest and most curved.
It's D. The first ribs.
Why it matters: they're the top pair, tucked under the collarbones.
